catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds a single persistent ROS geometry_msgs/Twist publication whose upstream callback has no acknowledgement, no duration and no measured distance/heading. cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 requires a bounded duration and distance/heading output, which the /cmd_vel callback does not provide; the receipt can only report transmission.

No catalogue class binds a posture service that only acknowledges the start of a one-second joint-target transition. cap.motion.home.v1 is joint homing with a different contract, and no class reports an unmeasured stand transition.
No catalogue class binds a posture service that only acknowledges the start of a one-second joint-target transition. The sit transition is not homing, a Cartesian pose, or a measured stop.

No catalogue class binds the fixed lie-down posture service. The sensed stop sends it as a request step, but the service only acknowledges that the lie transition started. cap.motion.stop.v1 requires a measured stopped state, which this service result does not provide.

No catalogue class binds a body-height offset service whose callback only validates a range and stores the value. cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 is an arm Cartesian pose with a different unit and output contract.

PASS on the fake backend: G1-G9 pass, evidence contract_checked, gate digest sha256:b7d0c44011e253aa069b5f5f2fa2463cd4ab4da16d821accd430b8d45bc4170c. The package is a configuration-only RosDriver for the pinned Webots ROS 2 Spot plug-in; it declares no Python native class and never imports the clone. Scope: the /cmd_vel geometry_msgs/msg/Twist subscription, the /joint_states sensor_msgs/msg/JointState and /Spot/odometry nav_msgs/msg/Odometry observations, the /Spot/stand_up, /Spot/sit_down and /Spot/lie_down SpotMotion services, and the /Spot/set_height SpotHeight service. The primary base control is the unacknowledged /cmd_vel publication: its callback stores previous_cmd_vel and converts linear.x, linear.y and angular.z into persistent gait state, with no acknowledgement and no stale-command timer in the clone. The receipt is therefore transmission-only (published=true, confirmed=false). The three velocity components have Limit.operator_required because the clone states no numeric envelope; site-limits.example.json is an illustrative operator overlay only and must be replaced. /Spot/set_height uses the source-stated [-0.2, 0.2] check at webots_spot/spot_driver.py:757. Safe state and the native e-stop binding are the fixed /Spot/lie_down request with override=true. The callback sets fixed_motion before its previous_cmd/override check and starts a one-second lie [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked every endpoint and type (absolute names, spot_driver.py:194-220; SpotMotion and SpotHeight are defined in the separate webots_spot_msgs repository and the override, answer and height fields match the callbacks), the set_height bound (757), the operator_required Twist bounds, all 20 facts and the stop. The e-stop and safe-state action were /Spot/lie_down with override=true, whose callback only stores fixed_motion and the lie targets and answers 'lying down' at once (662-672), while the step loop runs float_motion whenever /Spot/float_mode has set float mode, before it checks fixed_motion (935-948), and that path keeps moving the base by the last /cmd_vel (769-933); any later /cmd_vel or gait input also clears fixed_motion (363, 404), so the SDK would report a completed e-stop for a robot that keeps moving; five facts also said more than their lines (the float-mode 'so it is not a stop' clause, the defined_motions claim about the service, the blocksworld 'not a world reset' remark, a joint count and finite differences off their ranges). Reviewer removed the e-stop binding and safe_state=True and rewrote safe_state, the docstring, comments, the lie-down description, those facts and the step-loop and float_motion facts, added three source facts (float_mode default and SetBool service, the GaitInput callback, the SpotArm launch) and five fidelity gaps in driver.py, changed test_driver.py (the e-stop calls no posture service and fails MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held), updated facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate now fails G6.ESTOP_FAILED and, because the package is R2, G8 SAFE-028 (the same missing stop); the nine package cases pass, and collect.py reports RESULT_UNTRUSTED until the orchestrator writes status blocked. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence AGPL-3.0); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: No acknowledged stop: lie_down is a posture request acknowledged before any motion; float mode, which any client sets through /Spot/float_mode, bypasses it and keeps the base gliding at the last /cmd_vel, and any /cmd_vel or gait input (nav2 from nav_launch.py publishes /cmd_vel) resumes walking. The SDK performs safety_bindings.estop and then .safe_state, so lie_down followed by float_mode false would remove the float bypass, but both are callback-acknowledged mode requests without sensed completion, which the user's decision of 2026-11-04 does not accept; unblocking needs that decision revisited or an acknowledged Webots pause. Broken upstream code at the pin: with arena2 true SpotDriver.init uses self.spot_rotation before assigning it (spot_driver.py:144-146, 158); a refused stand, sit or lie request still sets fixed_motion (639, 651, 663). While Webots is paused every command waits 2 s for the resource reads and the services go unanswered. Licence AGPL-3.0, publish_review required.

MODEL REVIEW (grok-4.7, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): PASS after repair; the blocked text above is historical. Sensed-confirmation stop (SAFE-049, simulated only): /Spot/float_mode data false (spot_driver.py:220, callback 763-767), then /Spot/lie_down override true (662-672). Achieved only on three consecutive fresh /Spot/odometry samples still in x, y and orientation and inside the operator lying band. The check is quaternion span_max, not twist: the second publish can be a zero finite difference (571-573). The SetBool flag and the answer are not the stop. While fixed_motion is set, defined_motions calls handle_transforms_and_odometry (702) and step calls it again (950). The first call stores previous_rotation and does not publish odometry (558-560); it still publishes joint states. Once previous_rotation exists, both calls publish odometry and assign header.stamp from getTime() (478-481, assigned at 577). This repair reads that pair as one stamp. The clone has no line that says getTime() stays fixed, and its Python contains no robot.step. History is volatile; the publisher depth is 1 at line 201. throttle_ms 100 is rosbridge throttle_rate with queue_length 1: a waiting copy is overwritten, a late copy is forwarded, and the equal stamp fails closed. The fake models that clock. honor_throttle false stays sensed_stale (duplicate, seen 15). Thresholds are operator_required; the fixture is fake-only. min_span_ms 200 matches the fake's 100 ms ticks. A 32 ms producer needs a lower min_span_ms in simulation_deployment['estop_confirmation']. A step slower than max_gap_ms, or the one-second lie past confirm_within_ms, fails closed until those two bounds are raised. throttle_ms stays on the declaration. previous_cmd_vel is not cleared. No re-enable and no Webots pause. Float mode true, /cmd_vel and gait input can move the base again. nav_launch.py:37-50 includes nav2_bringup; this clone's nav2_params.yaml has no cmd_vel string, so this review does not state that nav2 publishes /cmd_vel. SpotArm is not stopped. Risk stays R2. AGPL-3.0, publish_review required.
